newsitem.title: GERMANY: World 96/97 cottonseed output down at 34.2 mln T.
newsitem.headline: World 96/97 cottonseed output down at 34.2 mln T.

text.p: Global cottonseed production in 1996/97 was seen falling to 34.2 million tonnes, down 1.1 million from last season, the independent Oil World newsletter said.
The publication also said crushings would decline by three percent over last season to 26.8 million tonnes.
Lower production in China, Greece, the former Soviet Union, Sudan, Brazil and Australia would more than offset output gains in India, Pakistan and the United States.
Australia would be the largest 96/97 cottonseed exporter, accounting for 210,000 tonnes (161,000 in 95/96) out of a 710,000 tonne world total (up from 705,000 in 95/96).
In cottonseed products, cotton oil output was forecast at 4.01 million tonnes after 4.11 million in 95/96 and 96/97 consumption was put at 4.04 million (4.10 million 95/96).
Oil World did not expect higher cotton oil prices, which it said would follow firm soy oil, to discourage global exports in 96/97, which it believed may rise by 10,000 tonnes to 255,000.
Cotton meal output was seen at 15.47 million tonnes (15.93 million 95/96) and consumption, concentrated in producer countries, at 15.55 million (15.90 million previously).
China, although reducing overall domestic consumption, would free up more meal for use at home by curbing exports.
